Are You Eligible for Workers’ Compensation in Colorado?

The first option for financial compensation after a workplace accident in Thornton is typically a workers’ compensation claim. Workers’ compensation is a program that is available to most employees in Colorado. It pays for a worker’s medical bills, two-thirds of their lost wages, occupational therapy, and other costs connected to a workplace injury or illness without requiring proof of fault or negligence. To be eligible for workers’ compensation benefits, you must be an employee – not an independent contractor – and you must report the accident to your employer within 10 days.
Personal Injury Lawsuits for Workplace Accidents in Thornton

While workers’ compensation can make it easy to obtain a monetary recovery for your occupational injury, it might not be the best option. Accepting a workers’ comp settlement takes away your right to hold an employer accountable for your injury. If your employer is guilty of an act or omission that contributed to your accident, such as a lack of proper employee training or a dangerous workplace, a lawsuit against your employer may result in greater financial compensation than workers’ comp.

If a third party – someone other than your employer – contributed to your accident, you may be able to file both a workers’ compensation claim and a personal injury lawsuit.
